title: Roman numerals
blurb: Read and write Roman numerals up to 3,999 with the seven symbols, the six subtractive pairs and the three-in-a-row rule, and do arithmetic by converting first.
question: A hospital cornerstone reads MCMXCVIII. In what year was it laid, and how would the year 2,049 be written in Roman numerals?

teach.body: Formally, Roman numerals are a non-positional number system: seven capital letters stand for fixed values, and a numeral's value is the sum of its symbols, except that a smaller symbol written just before a larger one is subtracted. In plain English: read left to right and add, but when a small symbol sits in front of a bigger one, take it away instead. There is no zero and no place value, so position only matters for that one subtracting rule.

head: Symbol
Value
Memory hook
teach.caption: Always write Roman numerals in capitals. Each step alternates × 5 and × 2: 1, 5, 10, 50, 100, 500, 1,000.

teach.body: 1. Largest to smallest, add: LXVI = 50 + 10 + 5 + 1 = 66. 2. A smaller symbol BEFORE a larger one is subtracted, but only in six pairs: IV (4), IX (9), XL (40), XC (90), CD (400), CM (900). Only I, X and C are ever subtracted. 3. I, X, C and M may repeat up to three times in a row; V, L and D never repeat. So 4 is IV, not IIII, and 100 is C, not LL.

teach.caption: Thousands are M, MM, MMM. To write any number up to 3,999, write each place from this table and join them.

items: 1,949: 1,000 = M, 900 = CM, 40 = XL, 9 = IX. Answer: MCMXLIX.
2,476: 2,000 = MM, 400 = CD, 70 = LXX, 6 = VI. Answer: MMCDLXXVI.
Arithmetic: XXXVI + XLVIII = 36 + 48 = 84 = LXXXIV. Convert, compute, convert back.

teach.caption: Split the numeral into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones first. A pair where the left symbol is smaller is ONE value.
I comes only before V and X; X only before L and C; C only before D and M.

teach.body: Aaliyah, a nursing applicant, notices MCMXCVIII on her hospital's cornerstone. Split it: M = 1,000; CM = 900; XC = 90; VIII = 8. Total: 1998. In 2026 the building is 2026 - 1998 = 28 years old, which would be written XXVIII. To write 2,049: MM (2,000) + XL (40) + IX (9) = MMXLIX. Reading CM as 1,100 would have given a year that has not happened yet: a quick sense check.

teach.text: The four classic slips: reading a subtractive pair as a sum (XC as 110, CD as 600), inventing a non-standard pair (IL for 49, VC for 95, IM for 999), repeating a symbol four times (XXXX, IIII), and subtracting two symbols at once (IIX). Writing digit by digit from the place table avoids all four.

items: Subtract only in IV, IX, XL, XC, CD, CM; only I, X and C are subtracted.
I, X, C, M repeat up to three times; V, L, D never repeat.
Write place by place (thousands, hundreds, tens, ones) and join.
For arithmetic, convert to ordinary numbers, compute, then convert back.

summary: You can now read any Roman numeral up to 3,999 by splitting it into places and spotting the subtractive pairs, and write any number in standard form. You can also add, subtract, multiply and divide numerals by converting first.

whyNot.0: XLIV = 40 + 4 = 44; 60 is LX, with the L first.
whyNot.2: LXVI = 66; 4 is IV, with the I before the V.
whyNot.3: I may not repeat four times; 4 is written IV.

whyNot.1: This reads IV as 6; I before V is subtracted, so IV = 4.
whyNot.2: This reads XL as 60; X before L is subtracted, so XL = 40.
whyNot.3: This reads both XL and IV as sums (60 and 6).

A.q: Which symbol is never written before a larger symbol to subtract?
A.why: V, L and D are never subtracted. 95 is XCV, not VC.

whyNot.0: I is subtracted in IV (4) and IX (9).
whyNot.1: X is subtracted in XL (40) and XC (90).
whyNot.2: C is subtracted in CD (400) and CM (900).

B.why: 1,000 = M, 400 = CD, 90 = XC, 2 = II. Together: MCDXCII.

whyNot.0: C may not repeat four times; 400 is written CD.
whyNot.1: DC = 600, so MDCXCII = 1,692; 400 is CD, with the C first.
whyNot.3: X may not repeat four times; 90 is written XC.

B.q: What is XXVII + XVIII, written as a Roman numeral?
B.why: XXVII = 27 and XVIII = 18. 27 + 18 = 45 = XL + V = XLV.

whyNot.0: LV = 55; 45 needs X before L (XL = 40), then V.
whyNot.1: V is never subtracted; 45 is written XLV.
whyNot.3: X may not repeat four times; 40 is written XL.

B.q: Which list orders these numerals from least to greatest?

whyNot.1: This reads XLIX and XCIX additively (as 71 and 121), so they land after LI and CI.
whyNot.2: XCIX = 99 is greater than LI = 51, so it cannot come second.
whyNot.3: This puts 99 and 101 first; XLIX (49) and LI (51) are smaller.

C.q: A clinic opened in MCMXC and closed in MMXXIV. For how many years was it open?

whyNot.0: This reads XC as 110, so the opening year looks like 2010.
whyNot.1: This reads XC as 110 and IV as 6 (2026 - 2010).
whyNot.3: This reads IV as 6, so the closing year looks like 2026.

C.why: 2,000 = MM, 400 = CD, 40 = XL, 4 = IV. Together: MMCDXLIV.

whyNot.2: C may not repeat four times; 400 is written CD.

C.q: Which is the standard Roman numeral for 990?

whyNot.0: X is subtracted only from L or C, never from M.
whyNot.2: X may not repeat four times; 90 is written XC.
whyNot.3: C may not repeat four times; 900 is written CM.

reteach.title: Think of telling time
reteach.question: People say "ten to six" to mean 5:50. How does that everyday habit explain the subtracting rule in Roman numerals?

blocks.body: When someone says "ten to six," the smaller amount comes first and is taken away from the bigger one: 6:00 minus 10 minutes. Roman numerals do the same thing. IX is "one before ten," so 10 - 1 = 9. XC is "ten before a hundred," 90. But "ten past six" puts the small amount after, and it is added, just as XI is 10 + 1 = 11 and CX is 110.

blocks.h: Before means minus, after means plus

blocks.text: Nobody says "one to fifty" to mean 49: the subtracting rule only uses the next two larger symbols. 49 is XLIX (40 + 9), never IL.

explain.body: I = 1, V = 5, X = 10, L = 50, C = 100, D = 500, M = 1,000. The fives (V, L, D) sit halfway between the ones, tens and hundreds.

test.q: Which Roman numeral symbol stands for 500?

explain.body: Symbols from largest to smallest are added. I, X, C and M may appear up to three times in a row, so 3 = III and 30 = XXX, but 4 and 40 need a subtractive pair.

whyNot.0: Only one symbol may be subtracted at a time; 8 is VIII, not IIX.
whyNot.2: VIIII = 9 with four repeats; 8 is VIII.

explain.body: IV 4, IX 9, XL 40, XC 90, CD 400, CM 900. Each pair is read as ONE value: the larger symbol minus the smaller one.

test.q: What is the value of CM?

whyNot.0: This adds C and M; a smaller symbol before a larger one is subtracted.

explain.body: Break the number into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones, write each from the place table, and join them: 1,904 = M + CM + IV = MCMIV (no tens).

test.why: 1,000 = M, 900 = CM, 0 tens, 4 = IV. Together: MCMIV.

whyNot.2: C may not repeat four times; 900 is written CM.
whyNot.3: I may not repeat four times; 4 is written IV.
